title: “You Know, Survive Basically?”: A Qualitative Examination on Food and Housing Insecurity and Victimization Risk in the Disability Community
abstract: People with an intellectual or developmental disability (IDD) are victimized at much higher rates than those without disabilities. Housing and food insecurity also contribute to an increased likelihood of experiencing victimization. This study will look at how unmet needs related to food and housing shape victimization among people with IDD. Based upon interview and focus group data from the disability community and service providers (e.g., disability advocates; law enforcement), we found that basic need insecurity affects the daily routines of individuals with an IDD and their available decisions. Accumulated needs may cause individuals to make changes to how they live (e.g., changes in living arrangements and/or service delivery), and these changes may create new opportunities for victimization.
